title: Quantifying earthquake-induced building damage from VIIRS nighttime lights: A multi-scale framework with deep learning–based area validation
abstract: Rapid and reliable assessment of earthquake-induced building damage is essential for effective emergency response, yet the quantitative relationship between nighttime light (NTL) variations observed by satellite sensors and physical structural damage remains insufficiently constrained by physically consistent validation. This study addresses this limitation by establishing a multi-scale analytical framework that explicitly links regional-scale VIIRS NTL observations (∼500 m resolution) with local, area-based building damage measurements derived from very high resolution (0.5 m) WorldView-2 imagery and deep learning–based semantic segmentation. Using the 2023 Türkiye earthquake as a case study, we introduce a VIIRS-based Normalized Difference Light Index (NDLI) to mitigate baseline luminosity heterogeneity and evaluate its relationship with two independent damage indicators: (i) the percentage of collapsed buildings obtained through visual interpretation, and (ii) an area-based Building Damage Index (BDI) computed from U-Net–based semantic segmentation of building footprints, which achieved an Intersection over Union (IoU) of 0.7819 and an F1-score of 0.8776 on the test dataset. Regression analysis reveals a distinct non-linear exponential relationship between NDLI and building damage severity, with a critical transition threshold at NDLI ≈ −0.3, beyond which damage indicators increase sharply. The area-based BDI demonstrates a stronger correspondence with NDLI variations (R 2 = 0.640, p < 0.001) than the count-based collapse metric (R 2 = 0.578, p < 0.001), consistent with the radiometric principle that satellite-measured radiance responds primarily to the spatial extent of illuminated structures rather than their numerical count. These results demonstrate that VIIRS-derived NDLI serves as a physically interpretable proxy for rapid, large-scale assessment of earthquake-induced building damage when validated using area-based metrics, while acknowledging that the derived empirical relationships are specific to the study area conditions and require multi-event validation for broader applicability.

title: Feature selection from Multi-Angular TECIS data for forest biomass estimation using a Model-driven sensitivity analysis approach
abstract: Forest ecosystems play a critical role in maintaining global carbon storage and regulating climate, with above-ground biomass (AGB) serving as a key indicator of forest carbon stocks. Optical remote sensing has become an essential data source for regional-scale, seamless mapping and multi-scale spatial extrapolation of forest AGB. The Terrestrial Ecosystem Carbon Inventory Satellite (TECIS), equipped with multi-angle optical sensors, provides abundant directional canopy observation information; however, the application potential and effective utilization of these multi-angle data remain systematically understudied. To address these challenges, this study proposes a novel framework for identifying AGB-sensitive features by integrating Copula–Shapley sensitivity analysis, allometric equation-constrained projection, and robustness analysis. First, the LESS model was used to simulate TECIS multi-angle reflectance data. Based on these simulations, a high-fidelity XGBoost surrogate model and an R-Vine Copula joint probability model for the input forest structural parameters were constructed. The Copula model preserved the inherent dependencies among forest structural parameters to perform conditional sampling. Combined with the surrogate model to predict multi-angle remote sensing responses, we calculated the conditional Shapley sensitivity of each structural parameter to remote sensing features under dependent conditions. Subsequently, leveraging a projection operator derived from forest allometric equations, the sensitivity of these structural parameters was mapped into the AGB space, thereby constructing a comprehensive AGB sensitivity index ( ϕ AGB ). Finally, a bootstrap-resampling-based robustness analysis was applied, using the criterion that the lower bound of the 95 % confidence interval must be greater than zero ( CI 2.5 % > 0) to adaptively screen for highly significant and stable AGB-sensitive features. The results show that 17 AGB-sensitive features were successfully identified, with their comprehensive sensitivity index ( ϕ ¯ AGB ) ranging from 0.0208 to 0.0712 and the coefficient of variation (CV) spanning 11.5 % to 37.5 %. Multi-angle features demonstrated a distinct advantage in sensitivity ranking: among the top 10 most sensitive features, 9 originated from multi-angle observations, and the top 5 were exclusively multi-angle features. Specifically, the angle-normalized index in the red band, AngND_B3_0°_b19° ( ϕ ¯ AGB = 0.0712 , CV = 11.5 %) and AngRat_B3_0°_b19° ( ϕ ¯ AGB = 0.0645 , CV = 13.6 %), exhibited the highest sensitivity and the best statistical stability. An AGB retrieval model was constructed using the LESS simulation dataset and validated against 32 field plots. The validation results revealed that the XGBoost model combined with features selected via the Copula-Shapley framework achieved the best AGB retrieval performance (R 2 = 0.754, RMSE = 12.950 t/ha). This performance significantly outperformed feature selection methods such as LASSO (R 2 = 0.698, RMSE = 14.334 t/ha), Mutual Information (R 2 = 0.665, RMSE = 15.109 t/ha)), and Pearson correlation analysis (R 2 = 0.629, RMSE = 15.890 t/ha)), while also demonstrating superiority over random forest and exponential regression models. Overall, this study fully unleashes the structural information advantages of TECIS multi-angle observations for forest AGB retrieval. The proposed AGB-sensitive feature extraction framework provides a valuable theoretical reference for the exploitation and feature construction of TECIS multi-angle data.

title: BAM: A physics-informed self-supervised framework for near-real-time wildfire burned area mapping from multi-source earth observation
abstract: The operational monitoring of global wildfires is frequently constrained by the latency of supervised training data generation and the radiometric challenges of distinguishing charred biomass from natural dark surface features. To address these limitations, this study presents the Burn Area Mapper (BAM), a fully automated, physics-informed machine learning framework implemented in Google Earth Engine. The framework employs a Physics-Informed Self-Supervision paradigm that eliminates the need for manual annotation by leveraging combustion stoichiometry to generate scene-specific training labels. Central to this approach is the novel Automated Temporal Burn Index (ATBI), which uses multiplicative scaling of NIR and SWIR bands to enforce a strict bimodal distribution, enabling an adaptive Otsu algorithm to isolate high-confidence burn signals automatically. These physics-derived labels are refined using a Gradient Tree Boost (GTB) classifier that incorporates textural and topographic features. We validated the framework across 15 wildfire events spanning 6 continents, achieving a global mean F1-score of 0.994 without regional retraining. Comparative benchmarking against the MODIS MCD64A1 product revealed that BAM captures up to 93% more burned area in fragmented landscapes. Furthermore, validation against 3-meter PlanetScope imagery (R2 = 0.80) confirms that BAM's probabilistic output effectively proxies sub-pixel burn fraction, resolving fine-scale fire fronts and unburned refugia invisible to coarse-resolution systems. By automating the production of high-precision burn maps in near-real time using robust atmospheric inversion (SREM), BAM offers a scalable, open-source solution for disaster response and post-fire ecological assessment.

title: From pixels to vectorized cadastral boundaries: Deep learning-based automated delineation of property boundaries in the Netherlands
abstract: Cadastral mapping remains one of the most resource-intensive components of land administration, while large parts of the world still lack complete and up-to-date cadastral information. In this context, remote sensing and deep learning can support the rapid production of initial cadastral boundaries for semi-automated mapping workflows. We present CadNet , a deep learning architecture for extracting initial cadastral boundaries from very high-resolution aerial imagery. The model is evaluated at the national scale in the Netherlands using a large and geographically diverse subset of the CadastreVision benchmark and is compared with eight baseline networks under identical experimental conditions. CadNet consistently achieves the highest F1 scores across all evaluated landscapes (mixed: 0.502, rural: 0.468, and peri-urban: 0.556), outperforming the next-best models by 1.3%–1.7%, and produces the least fragmented vector output, reducing the connected-component ratio by 8%–26% relative to the best-performing baseline. Qualitative results further show more continuous boundary representations and better recovery of partially occluded visible boundaries. These findings demonstrate that connectivity-aware, multi-scale deep learning can improve the extraction of initial cadastral boundaries over large areas from aerial imagery.

title: Satellite embeddings for crop type classification: a comparative examination
abstract: Embedding datasets encode complex relationships among multiple sources of Earth observation data into a compact format. Here, we evaluated the utility of a 10-m global Satellite Embedding product (SE) for classifying crop types in central California for the year 2020. We compared the classification accuracy of a random forest model based exclusively on the SE layer to an existing random forest model with multiple imagery inputs. Our results showed the SE-based classification had higher agreement with the reference dataset (California Department of Water Resources crop map) than the classification based on Landsat and National Agricultural Imagery Program inputs (94.7% versus. 91.9% overall accuracy, respectively). The performance of individual crop types was consistent across models, ranging from high agreement for rice (98.4% versus 98% accuracy) to lower agreement for pasture, grain, and fallow/young perennial classes (< 65% accuracy in both models). The SE-based workflow used three times less cloud-based computational resources and represented substantial savings of predictor development time. Geospatial embedding products can aid classification efforts by reducing predictor development time and processing demands while maintaining classification accuracy.

title: Deep learning models for estimating volume and Lorey’s height across Nordic countries using optical and SAR satellite images
abstract: Spatially explicit information on forest resources and structure is essential for sustainable forest management and evidence-based policy-making. In the Nordic region, large-scale forest mapping often relies on integrating National Forest Inventory (NFI) field plots with airborne laser scanning (ALS) data. However, infrequent nationwide ALS campaign coverage limits their use for continuous monitoring. Satellite imagery, with its high temporal and spatial resolution, provides a promising alternative. We evaluate UNet-based deep learning models trained on wall-to-wall ALS-derived forest resource maps for predicting volume and Lorey’s height in Norway using optical (Sentinel-2) and SAR (Sentinel-1, PALSAR-2) data. The UNet models, trained on both Finnish and Norwegian ALS maps, are benchmarked against extreme gradient boosting (XGB) models. Transfer learning is further explored by finetuning models using Norwegian NFI plots. Model accuracies are assessed using 541 reserved test NFI plots and 44 independent forest stands, representing high‑volume mature boreal forests (>200 m 3 ha −1 ). The UNet model trained on Norwegian ALS‑based data achieved R2 values of 0.59 for both volume and Lorey’s height when evaluated on NFI plots, and 0.70 and 0.59 for forest stands, respectively, outperforming the XGB models. Finetuning improved model transferability, yielding gains of up to 0.13 in R2 for volume and 0.46 for Lorey’s height when adapting the Finnish model to Norwegian conditions. Utilizing SAR data alongside optical data enhanced model accuracy. Overall, our findings demonstrate the potential of UNet models trained on wall-to-wall ALS maps for forest resource mapping across Nordic countries.

title: CDBNet: Detail-preserving and structure-aware pipeline mapping in chemical industrial parks
abstract: Accurate maps of chemical industrial park pipelines are important for infrastructure inventory, safety supervision, emergency response, and maintenance planning, yet pipeline networks are difficult to delineate from high-resolution optical images because they are narrow, low-texture, partially occluded, and embedded in visually complex industrial backgrounds. This study develops CDBNet, a detail-preserving and structure-aware deep network for pipeline mapping from Earth observation images. A frozen DINOv3 ViT-L backbone pretrained on satellite imagery is used as a transferable feature extractor. A cross-layer detail-preserving foundation pyramid adapter converts multi-layer transformer tokens into high-resolution pyramid features, a direction-aware aggregation module enhances elongated structures in horizontal, vertical, oblique, and curved layouts, and a boundary-skeleton-guided refinement module improves contour localization and centerline continuity. We also construct PipelineRS, a pixel-level annotated dataset from GF-2 and GF-7 images covering four chemical industrial parks in China. On PipelineRS, CDBNet achieves 0.9499 precision, 0.9365 recall, 0.9432 F1-score, 0.8925 foreground IoU, 0.9460 mean IoU, and 0.9029 average boundary localization accuracy. Cross-dataset tests on Massachusetts and DeepGlobe road datasets, robustness experiments, and independent cross-regional evaluations further show that the proposed method can produce stable geospatial information for slender industrial infrastructure mapping.

title: Enhanced retrieval of aerosol optical/microphysical parameters for Himawari-8 geostationary satellite measurements with data-driven deep learning method
abstract: The high temporal resolution of Himawari-8 (H8) geostationary satellite has distinctive advantages in capturing diurnal variation of aerosol properties. However, the operational H8 aerosol products including Aerosol Optical Depth (AOD) are subject to considerable uncertainties due to assumptions and simplified surface reflectance. To fully exploit the H8 multi-spectral measurements, a data-driven retrieval framework based on a Deep Belief Network (DBN) was developed to simultaneously retrieve aerosol optical and microphysical parameters. By directly modeling H8 spectral reflectance at the top of the atmosphere (TOA) with matched AERONET products in 82 sites across diverse surface types and emission sources, four aerosol parameters including AOD, fine and coarse AOD (FAOD and CAOD), and single scattering albedo (SSA) are retrieved. Ground-based validation shows that the H8 DBN retrievals achieve high accuracies for AOD and FAOD, with correlation coefficients of 0.935 and 0.930, respectively, substantially outperforming the operational JAXA product (R = 0.703 for AOD). The retrieved CAOD and SSA also show good agreement with AERONET observations. Comparisons with MODIS and JAXA H8 aerosol products show very high consistency in both spatial and temporal variations. H8 DBN retrievals can clearly distinguish biomass burning smoke and dust plumes by their particle size and absorption. Additionally, hourly H8 DBN retrievals accurately reflect diurnal variations of aerosol properties. Consequently, the developed DBN-based approach provides a flexible and robust retrieval method for dynamic aerosol properties over East Asia.

title: Deep learning-based burned area mapping of California wildfires using Sentinel-2 and Landsat-8 imagery enhanced with super-resolution techniques
abstract: The increasing frequency of wildfires under a changing climate has led to extensive ecosystem destruction, highlighting the need for reliable burned area assessment using satellite imagery. Single-satellite data are constrained by observation gaps and interference from smoke and clouds, whereas multi-satellite data fusion can mitigate these limitations. Nonetheless, the fusion techniques still encounter challenges such as spatial information loss from resolution differences and cross-satellite domain mismatch. This study presents a burned area mapping framework that integrates super-resolution (SR) with transfer learning to address spatial and domain gaps in multi-satellite data. Specifically, Landsat-8 imagery is super-resolved to 7.5 m resolution, and the pretrained model is subsequently fine-tuned using Sentinel-2 imagery. Additionally, we investigated spectral index expansion to improve detection performance. Applied to California wildfires from 2013 to 2023, the input band expansion achieved a Burned Intersection over Union (IoU) of 0.821 when multiple spectral indices were incorporated. The SR-based transfer learning approach further improved performance with a Burned IoU of 0.850, representing a 4.55 % enhancement over the original Landsat-8 pre-trained model (0.813). Validation on 2025 wildfires demonstrated consistent performance and model robustness. These results highlight that the proposed SR-based approach offers benefits beyond simple resolution enhancement in multi-satellite data fusion. Furthermore, they confirm that spectral index-based input expansion contributes to accuracy improvements. The proposed framework is expected to support disaster response and environmental monitoring applications.

title: Parameter-efficient multimodal adaptation of vision foundation models for remote sensing semantic segmentation
abstract: Multimodal remote sensing semantic segmentation improves scene understanding by integrating complementary information from heterogeneous Earth observation data. Although pretrained Vision Foundation Models (VFMs) provide strong general-purpose representations, adapting them to multimodal tasks typically requires updating large modality-specific encoders, and optimization tends to be dominated by the optical modality, leaving auxiliary cues under-utilized. To address these challenges, we propose MoBaNet, a parameter-efficient multimodal adaptation framework that keeps the VFM backbone frozen and concentrates trainable capacity on three complementary components. First, the Cross-modal Prompt-Injected Adapter (CPIA) generates semantic prompts from paired modalities and injects them into lightweight bottleneck adapters to enable cross-modal interaction under the frozen backbone. Second, the Difference-Guided Gated Fusion Module (DGFM) exploits cross-modal discrepancy to guide channel-wise and spatially adaptive feature fusion. Third, the training-only Modality-Conditional Random Masking (MCRM) strategy locally corrupts one modality at a time and applies hard-pixel auxiliary supervision to modality-specific branches, encouraging more robust use of complementary cues. Extensive experiments on the ISPRS Vaihingen and Potsdam benchmarks show that MoBaNet achieves the best overall performance among the compared methods, while its default DINOv2-ViT-B configuration uses only 5.43% trainable parameters and remains robust under partial modality degradation.

title: Physics-Guided Machine learning approach for estimating spatiotemporally seamless FAPAR from Landsat surface reflectance
abstract: Fraction of Absorbed Photosynthetically Active Radiation (FAPAR) is a key biophysical parameter for characterizing vegetation photosynthetic efficiency, playing a crucial role in understanding terrestrial ecosystems, global carbon cycles, and climate change impacts. While satellite observations enable global-scale FAPAR estimation, existing medium to low-resolution products (250 m-1 km) cannot adequately capture surface heterogeneity, particularly in regions with complex terrain and diverse vegetation types. This study presents a novel physics-informed machine learning approach for high-resolution FAPAR retrieval. First, we established a coupled soil-vegetation-atmosphere radiative transfer model to simulate Landsat surface reflectance and FAPAR at global representative pixels. Second, we integrated simulated reflectance-simulated FAPAR and actual reflectance-actual FAPAR to construct a physics-informed Light Gradient Boosting Machine (PILGBM) for retrieving clear-sky FAPAR from Landsat surface reflectance. Third, we incorporated spatio-temporal constraints and environmental variables to build a second LGBM model for reconstructing missing Landsat FAPAR under cloudy conditions. The method was validated against ground measurements, including Ground Based Observations for Validation (GBOV) and ImagineS, achieving high spatial-temporal consistency (GBOV: R² = 0.793, RMSE = 0.113 and ImagineS: R² = 0.856, RMSE = 0.110) and demonstrating robust performance across diverse landscapes. This approach effectively addresses the limitations of traditional methods regarding insufficient physical constraints and cloud contamination, while providing continuous 30 m-resolution FAPAR products at 16-day intervals. The resulting high-resolution FAPAR dataset offers valuable support for studying ecosystem light use efficiency, simulating vegetation productivity, and assessing carbon cycle dynamics.

title: A spatiotemporal framework for identifying urban flood priority areas in megacities using social media data
abstract: Urban flood (UF) poses major challenges to sustainable development and public safety. Geographic information-based studies commonly apply machine learning (ML) with UF samples and multi-domain factors to assess urban flood susceptibility (UFS) and identify priority regions for UF management. However, most existing approaches rely solely on the latest UFS map, overlooking the dynamic nature of UF and thereby reducing the reliability of the identified priority areas. To address this limitation, we propose an ML-based framework for spatiotemporal UFS estimation to delineate more accurate and practical UF priority regions. The framework integrates: (1) Natural Language Processing to extract flood locations from social media ( Weibo) , and (2) a Spatiotemporal Susceptibility Extraction (SSE) method that combines the spatial and temporal characteristics of UFS. Guangzhou, a megacity in China with frequent UF events and extensive Weibo usage, is employed as the case study. We found: (1) incorporating UF locations extracted from social media effectively complements official records, as evidenced by both the increased information content of the positive class across multiple flood-conditioning factors and the improved classifier performance and robustness; and (2) compared with priority areas directly delineated from the latest-year UFS map, the SSE-derived UF priority areas show higher accuracy when evaluated against ground-truth UF data, further supported by high-resolution remote sensing imagery, while also exhibiting more spatially concentrated and continuous patterns. The proposed framework enables rapid and reliable identification of UF priority areas and provides practical decision support for UF prevention and management in rapidly urbanizing megacities under resource constraints.

title: Improving text–image alignment for referring remote sensing image segmentation guided by vision foundation model
abstract: The task of referring remote sensing image segmentation (RRSIS) aims to predict segmentation masks of target objects based on text descriptions. Effective alignment between textual and visual modalities is crucial for achieving high performance. However, most existing RRSIS methods overlook the inherent domain gap between the two modalities and naively fuse visual and text features. Moreover, they lack guidance from domain-specific priors during alignment, often leading to inaccurate segmentation results. In this paper, we propose a novel method for RRSIS, namely TIANet. This method combines implicit and explicit alignment approaches to achieve fine-grained image-text alignment. Furthermore, to compensate for the lack of domain priors during alignment, we leverage the Remote Sensing Vision Foundation Model (RS-VFM) to guide both alignment strategies. On one hand, the Prior-Guided Visual-Text Feature Alignment Module (PVTAM) leverages domain priors to fuse textual and visual features in a stage-wise manner, thereby achieving cross-modal implicit alignment at the feature level. On the other hand, the Dynamic Bidirectional Alignment and Prior Distillation (DBAPD) loss is adopted to implement explicit cross-modal alignment during training. Furthermore, to enhance the perception ability of small targets, the Kernel-Adaptive Small Target Enhancement Module (KASTEM) is used in the decoder stage. Extensive experiments on the RefSegRS and RRSIS-D datasets show that our TIANet achieves excellent performance compared with other advanced methods, with a 1.22% mIoU improvement over existing state-of-the-art approaches on the RefSegRS dataset.

title: PLGCA-SAM: Progressive local and global context-aware network incorporating SAM for remote sensing crop mapping
abstract: Precise crop mapping via remote sensing is critical for the rational utilization of cultivated land resources. Remote sensing techniques and deep learning-based semantic segmentation methods provide effective approaches to large-scale crop mapping. However, due to variations among remote sensing imaging systems, significant distributional shifts exist across different remote sensing datasets, which limit the generalizability of deep learning models. To address the issue, we propose a semantic segmentation network named PLGCA-SAM for crop mapping in remote sensing imagery. PLGCA-SAM integrates the contextual perception capability of PLGCA with the powerful generalization of SAM. Specifically, we introduce a task-adaptive encoding (TAE) module, which includes a SAM adapter to align SAM’s generic visual features with the PLGCA feature space, and a task-guided mechanism that refines the fused representation using a task-aware loss. This design enables more effective feature integration and improves adaptability across diverse remote sensing datasets. Experiments conducted on GF-2 and Sentinel-2 datasets demonstrate that PLGCA-SAM achieves 2.03% and 1.50% improvements in mIoU, respectively, over SOTA methods. Our code will be obtained by: https://github.com/Hanhlab/PLGCA-SAM.git .

title: Filtering GEDI footprints based on combined spatial-spectral characteristics for individual building height mapping in 12 major global cities
abstract: Building height is an essential variable for describing the urban vertical landscape and evaluating urban resilience to natural disasters and climate change adaptation. Building-scale height maps are key to quantifying urban structures across multiple relevant scales (e.g., building, block, and landscape scales). Although some studies have filled in missing building height data using various methods, the scarcity of temporally consistent and spatially balanced building height samples continues to limit mapping accuracy. This is particularly true in the Global South, where urban vertical data remain scarce. In this study, we developed an easy-to-use mapping framework to produce building-scale heights for global major cities in 2020 by combining active and passive remotely sensed data. Specifically, we proposed a novel approach for generating building-scale height samples through integrating Global Ecosystem Dynamics Investigation (GEDI) data and building footprints. Combining spatial-spectral characteristics effectively mitigated the impact of positional offsets in GEDI footprints during sample construction. Twelve cities at different stages of development were selected as the study area. Validation results indicated good agreement between derived samples and reference data ( r = 0.87; RMSE = 5.78 m). Random forest models calibrated with local samples, neighboring high-value samples, and variables derived from building footprints as well as Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 data produced accurate building height maps ( r = 0.81; RMSE = 11.48 m). Our framework outperforms existing products in accuracy stability, alleviating the global scarcity of building-scale height samples. This contributes to building-scale height data availability and reliability.

title: GFS-Net: Geometry–frequency synergistic fusion for accurate optical–SAR land-cover classification
abstract: High-precision land-cover classification (LCC) from remote sensing imagery provides valuable semantic information. This information is critical for intelligent navigation and environmental understanding in autonomous unmanned systems. Optical imagery provides rich spectral and texture information, while synthetic aperture radar (SAR) offers all-weather sensing and strong structural characterization. The effective fusion of optical and SAR data plays a vital role in LCC, but it is hindered by heterogeneous imaging mechanisms that introduce geometric misalignment and frequency-domain discrepancies in the fusion process. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a geometry–frequency synergistic fusion network (GFS-Net) for accurate optical–SAR land-cover classification. By jointly integrating a Swin Transformer-based hierarchical dual-stream encoder with a carefully designed decoder that incorporates semantic flow alignment and local-context embedding, GFS-Net enables accurate multi-scale feature alignment and fine-grained detail recovery. At the core of the network, a geometry–frequency synergistic fusion module explicitly combines deformable geometric alignment with frequency-domain amplitude-phase fusion. This module corrects cross-modal spatial offsets, suppresses SAR speckle noise, and preserves discriminative optical structures. Furthermore, a dual-domain gated recalibration module is introduced to adaptively suppress modality-specific redundancy and enhance complementary semantic responses through global gating and joint spatial–channel rectification. Extensive experiments on the WHU-OPT-SAR and DFC2025 datasets show that GFS-Net achieves 84.96% OA and 58.64% mIoU on WHU-OPT-SAR and 87.02% OA and 74.66% mIoU on DFC2025, outperforming the strongest compared method CFFormer by +1.14% and +0.44% mIoU, respectively.

title: A physics-guided transfer learning approach for atmospheric correction of low-altitude remote sensing at extreme zenith angles
abstract: Tower-based and other low-altitude hyperspectral remote sensing systems enable high-frequency water quality monitoring, complementing satellite observations. However, at extreme sensor zenith angles (>80°), which are required for expanded spatial coverage, existing atmospheric correction (AC) methods lack validation and exhibit reduced accuracy, creating a critical gap in near-surface aquatic remote sensing. To address this challenge, we propose a physics-guided transfer learning atmospheric correction (PGTL-AC) framework that integrates 3.11 million coupled 6S–HydroLight simulations with field measurements to bridge the simulation-to-reality gap. Validated across heterogeneous environments, i.e., the turbid Bahe River in Xi’an, China, and the high-aerosol coastal waters of the Dongtou Archipelago in Wenzhou, China, PGTL-AC achieves a mean absolute percentage difference (MAPD) < 8.5 % for visible-band (400–700 nm) remote sensing reflectance and maintains physically consistent performance (MAPD < 17.5 %) across the full spectral range (400–865 nm). For operational water quality monitoring, Secchi disk depth retrieval achieves an MAPD < 18 % in cross-regional validation. In summary, PGTL-AC addresses the AC bottleneck for tower-based aquatic remote sensing at extreme zenith angles, enabling real-time water-quality early warning and establishing high-quality validation sites for next-generation ocean color missions (e.g., NASA PACE and ESA Sentinel-3). The demonstrated accuracy is presently bounded by the validated conditions, namely two optically contrasting Case II water sites and aerosol loadings of AOT550 ≤ 0.8; performance outside this envelope requires further validation.

title: A novel method for estimating urban building heights using bi-temporal high resolution satellite imagery and reprojected nDSM
abstract: Information on multi-temporal building heights in urban areas is crucial for understanding vertical urbanization patterns. In particular, acquiring building height data for historical periods is of great significance for studying long-term urban land changes. However, existing deep learning-based methods for building height estimation from monocular (single-view) imagery face two key limitations that hinder the retrieval of historical building heights: the difficulty in directly deriving building heights from off-nadir imagery (i.e., images acquired at a tilted viewing angle), and the substantial degradation in accuracy when applied to cross-temporal height estimation, where no height data for the target time period are available. This study proposes a novel method for estimating building heights for a target temporal period using bi-temporal (target and reference dates) off-nadir high spatial resolution (HSR) satellite images and a local reprojected normalized Digital Surface Model (nDSM) from reference date. The method consists of three main stages: generation of bi-temporal Line-of-Sight nDSMs (Los-nDSMs), estimation of target-temporal building heights using a dual-attention-based conditional Generative Adversarial Network (DA-cGAN), and height calibration. The proposed method was evaluated in two study areas using bi-temporal HSR images and local height data derived from LiDAR point cloud data for a reference date. For the first study area, the main urban center of Beijing, WorldView-2 images were used, while for the second, Tongzhou New City, Beijing, Pleiades images were used. Averaged over the two study areas, the proposed method outperforms two state-of-the-art methods relying on single temporal imagery and nDSM. It reduces the mean absolute errors (MAEs) by 3.42 m and 2.24 m, and the root mean square errors (RMSEs) by 4.95 m and 4.35 m, respectively, relative to the two competitors, while achieving a zero-mean normalized cross-correlation (ZNCC) of 0.92. The proposed method provides an effective solution for estimating building heights across different temporal periods in urban areas, using HSR images with varying viewing angles and from different sensors. It is particularly valuable in scenarios where historical height data are unavailable.

title: Multimodal loess cave extraction using LMUNet-RCAM: Integrating hillshade and RGB features with local attention mechanisms
abstract: Loess caves (LCs), a typical type of micro-landform widely distributed across the Chinese Loess Plateau, constitute a significant geological hazard. Accurate identification of LCs is essential for mitigating risks to human life, infrastructure, and environment. However, the complex morphology and subtle topographic expression of LCs present substantial challenges for reliable detection. This study proposes LMUNet-RCAM, an improved global–local feature enhancement network that integrates hillshade information derived from Digital Elevation Models (DEMs) to improve representation robustness. To address the irregular spatial patterns of LCs, the network incorporates novel Local Transformer mMoBA(LM) to refine feature representations prior to their input into the U-Net backbone, thereby expanding the effective receptive field in both global and local contexts. Furthermore, a Recurrent Convolutional Attention Module (RCAM) is introduced to enhance spatial and channel-wise semantic discrimination. Within RCAM, Gated-Swin-RNN (G-S-R) is employed to reconstruct local feature sequences, improving network stability under complex terrain conditions. Extensive experiments on test area demonstrate that LMUNet-RCAM consistently outperforms existing state-of-the-art semantic segmentation methods in LCs detection.

title: Vegetation canopy height retrieval in complex mountainous regions based on data calibration and CNN model
abstract: Vegetation canopy height is a vital metric for quantifying aboveground biomass, evaluating ecosystem integrity, and informing forest management strategies, playing a pivotal role in climate change mitigation and sustainable forestry. However, accurate estimation of canopy height faces three major challenges: topographic complexity in mountainous regions, landscape spatial heterogeneity, and inherent limitations of spaceborne LiDAR systems (e.g., GEDI) in detecting low-stature vegetation. This study proposes a regional calibration approach for GEDI-derived height labels and integrates the calibrated labels with multi-source remote sensing data to retrieve canopy height at 10 m resolution. Key findings demonstrate that: (1) The calibration model that couples Random Forest Regression and Multiple Linear Regression can effectively mitigate GEDI’s overestimation of low-stature vegetation and provide reliable label data for subsequent canopy height mapping; (2) Among all feature combinations, optical imagery emerged as the most influential contributor to model performance, significantly improving predictive accuracy when included; (3) The optimized model achieves a mean absolute error (MAE) of 2.26 m against field measurements, showing strong consistency with airborne LiDAR validation (MAE = 2.63 m). Qualitative evaluations highlight the model’s heightened sensitivity to diverse land cover types, enabling more precise delineation of vegetation boundaries. The calibrated height labels further improve the characterization of canopy height across forest, shrub, and grassland areas. These results demonstrate the potential of GEDI label calibration combined with multi-source remote sensing data for large-scale canopy height mapping in complex mountainous regions.

title: Learning instance-level semantic Gaussian representations for occlusion-aware urban scene reconstruction from UAV imagery
abstract: UAV-based earth observation provides an efficient and flexible means for detailed urban geospatial modeling and digital twin construction. However, in complex urban environments, foreground occlusions caused by trees, vegetation, and other clutter frequently lead to incomplete structures, contaminated textures, and inconsistent observations across views, thereby reducing the quality and usability of reconstructed urban products. Existing methods still struggle in such scenarios, not only because of severe occlusion itself, but also because they lack a representation at the instance level that can explicitly distinguish target urban structures from occluding interference in 3D space. Without such a representation, Gaussian primitives tend to become entangled across semantic regions, which limits reliable separation between target urban structures and occluders, accurate boundary delineation, and consistent urban scene reconstruction across views from UAV imagery. To address this issue, this paper proposes a semantic Gaussian learning framework at the instance level, enhanced by foundation priors, for urban scene reconstruction from UAV imagery. Specifically, high-level semantic, segmentation, and structural priors extracted from vision foundation models are introduced to guide semantic Gaussian representation learning at the instance level in 3D space. On this basis, an Instance-level Semantic Gaussian Module is designed to inject prior-enhanced semantics into Gaussian primitives, enabling more discriminative representation learning at the instance level. Furthermore, a Prior-guided Interaction Module is developed to establish effective collaboration between visual prior features and 3D Gaussian representations, so that RGB appearance semantics and 3D spatial structure can be jointly encoded within a unified semantic and structural representation. Benefiting from this design, the learned Gaussian representation provides a reliable basis for instance separation, missing-region localization, and consistent urban scene reconstruction across views under severe occlusions. Experimental results on multiple datasets demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms representative baselines in instance separation accuracy, boundary quality, and rendering consistency. The results further show that the proposed representation effectively alleviates instance boundary overlap and category confusion, while improving the completeness, consistency, and usability of urban geospatial products derived from UAV imagery.

title: A two-stage transformer framework for reconstructing hourly 1 km all-weather land surface temperature using cross-scale transfer learning
abstract: High spatiotemporal resolution land surface temperature (LST) reconstruction is essential for analyzing land-atmosphere interactions and thermal environmental dynamics. Thermal infrared observations, the primary source of regional and global LST, are affected by cloud contamination, scale discrepancies, and distribution shifts. Meanwhile, reconstruction methods struggle to provide both hourly continuity and kilometer-scale detail, and cross-scale fusion often causes spatial over-smoothing. To address these limitations, we propose ST-LSTrans, a two-stage Transformer framework for reconstructing regional hourly 1 km all-weather LST. It uses cross-scale transfer learning with global pre-training on hourly ∼6.25 km CLDAS LST to capture regional thermodynamic evolution and local fine-tuning on four-times-daily 1000 m MODIS LST to recover kilometer-scale thermal heterogeneity. A KL divergence constraint is introduced to reduce distribution shifts and spatial over-smoothing during cross-scale fusion. Validation results based on multi-source datasets show that the global pre-training stage achieved an average RMSE of 1.13 K, while the local fine-tuning stage achieved an average RMSE of 1.06 K, with the minimum RMSE reaching 0.87 K. Independent Landsat validation showed that the reconstructed product achieved a scene-averaged RMSE of 2.98 K and improved upon the original CLDAS background field. Additional evaluations against VIIRS VNP21, which is generated using an independent temperature-emissivity separation algorithm, confirmed the cross-sensor consistency of the reconstructed LST. Ground-based observations further demonstrated that ST-LSTrans preserved realistic diurnal temperature cycle characteristics under both clear-sky and persistent cloudy conditions. SHAP analysis further revealed scale-dependent transitions in LST driving mechanisms from coarse-scale atmospheric forcing to kilometer-scale terrain and land surface controls. This study provides a unified and interpretable modelling framework for high spatiotemporal resolution LST reconstruction and driving mechanism analysis.

title: A spatiotemporal reconstruction framework for GRACE/GRACE-FO-derived groundwater storage anomalies based on historical phase-constrained gap filling and physics-guided global–local downscaling
abstract: Observations from the Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment (GRACE) and GRACE Follow-On (GRACE-FO) provide essential information on terrestrial water storage anomalies (TWSA), from which groundwater storage anomalies (GWSA) can be derived. However, the approximately 11-month mission gap and the coarse spatial resolution of the original products constrain their application in regional groundwater monitoring and water-resource assessment. This study developed an integrated spatiotemporal reconstruction framework for the Three-North Region of China by combining historical phase-constrained gap filling with physics-guided global–local downscaling. First, a Kling-Gupta Efficiency-based singular spectrum analysis method (KGC-SSA) was developed to reconstruct the mission gap without external forcing data. Second, a physics-guided global–local-residual geographically weighted extreme gradient boosting framework (GLR-GWXGB) was developed to downscale GWSA to 1 km under grid-wise coarse-scale consistency constraints. KGC-SSA yielded a mean ensemble reconstruction spread of 0.06 cm during the mission gap and performed broadly comparably to benchmark methods. Relative to the global benchmark model, GLR-GWXGB improved internal validation performance, preserved regional-scale consistency with the original GRACE-derived GWSA, and enhanced local spatial detail. Correlations with groundwater observations improved at more than 70% of monitoring sites. The reconstructed 1 km product further captured persistent groundwater-storage decline during 2002–2022, with intensified depletion after approximately 2012, while retaining the dominant long-term and seasonal characteristics of the original series. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides a robust approach for generating temporally continuous and spatially refined groundwater-storage information from GRACE/GRACE-FO observations.

title: Relaxing the clear-sky assumption: Cloud-tolerant spatiotemporal fusion via mask-guided feature modulation and temporal-memory collaboration
abstract: The precise characterization of dynamic Earth surface processes relies on time-series remote sensing imagery with both high spatial fidelity and frequent temporal coverage. While spatiotemporal fusion (STF) bridges this resolution trade-off by integrating complementary observations, its practical application remains constrained by the idealized ”clear-sky assumption”. This requirement often favors the selection of temporally distant cloud-free acquisitions over temporally closer but cloud-contaminated observations, potentially reducing the relevance of reference information. To address this limitation, we propose CloudSTF, a robust framework designed to achieve high-fidelity reconstruction by effectively exploiting partially occluded observations. Our approach employs a Mask-guided Multi-scale Swin Transformer (M 2 ST) encoder to capture cloud spatial patterns and suppress noise propagation during feature extraction. This is coupled with a Cross-temporal Memory-guided Fusion (CTMF) module that adaptively integrates temporal trends with textural details retrieved from a spatio-temporal memory bank. To validate this paradigm, we introduce the Global Cloud-shrouded Regions (GCR-STF) benchmark, a geographically distributed dataset comprising 24 representative agricultural and urban sites across six continents. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CloudSTF consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods. Additional assessments across varying cloud densities and diverse landscapes further demonstrate the robustness and applicability of CloudSTF under realistic cloud-contaminated conditions. These results suggest that CloudSTF provides a reliable solution for continuous Earth monitoring in realistic, cloud-prone environments. Source code and the GCR-STF benchmark are available at https://github.com/Sichen-Lu/CloudSTF .

title: Enhanced early warning of extreme river discharge events in the Yangtze River Basin using atmospheric circulation signals
abstract: Early warning of extreme river discharge events (ERDEs) is crucial for water resources management and disaster reduction in the Yangtze River Basin (YRB), yet substantial uncertainty remains in their prediction. This study proposes a novel strategy to enhance ERDE early warning by detecting its associated atmospheric circulation signals. We develop DetRF, a machine learning model that integrates anomaly detection with a balanced random forest ensemble. DetRF was trained and validated using ERA5 reanalysis data from 2000 to 2019 and independently applied to 2020–2024, with its early warning performance evaluated against satellite-based precipitation and reanalysis river discharge data. Across eight subregions of the YRB, DetRF effectively detects ERDE-related atmospheric circulation signals, achieving mean recall, precision, and F1 score values of 0.756, 0.506, and 0.576, respectively, and consistently outperforming benchmark machine learning models. The detected signals accurately capture key synoptic features associated with hydrological extremes, including the positions and intensities of troughs, vortices, and cyclones, as well as moisture transport. More than 99% of the detected signals are followed by precipitation within five days, while persistent precipitation occurs in over 67% of cases across both local and upstream regions. More importantly, an average of 93.8% of DetRF-detected circulation signals are followed by at least one ERDE within the subsequent five days. These findings establish a direct link between specific atmospheric circulation signals and subsequent hydrological extremes, offering a new pathway for extending ERDE early warning beyond conventional hydrological prediction. The proposed framework is particularly promising for regions where hydrological observations are sparse.

title: Topology-preserving river vectorization via HydroSAM and differentiable graph optimization under coarse labels
abstract: Accurate river-network extraction supports global hydrological management and environmental monitoring. Automated extraction from remote-sensing imagery remains challenging because river morphology is highly variable, fine tributaries have weak visual signals, canopy and infrastructure can obscure channels, and dense annotations are scarce or spatially incomplete. Conventional raster predictions can also be fragmented and lack structural continuity. We present HydroSAM, a three-stage framework for raster extraction and topology-aware vectorization. A frozen SAM 2 Hiera encoder is adapted with QV-LoRA and the proposed Directional Curvilinear Prior Injection (DCPI), while a gated Digital Elevation Model (DEM) branch contributes coarse-scale topographic context. Segmentation is produced in a zero-prompt setting by the native SAM 2 mask decoder. A graph-guided differentiable vectorization stage then converts probability maps into connected parametric river networks. We also present M2Hydro, a benchmark containing 7,947 high-resolution 4096 × 4096 source image-annotation pairs across China. In single-run tests, HydroSAM-MM attains an F1 of 0.6995 and clDice of 0.7753 on M2Hydro. The evaluations indicate that HydroSAM supports parameter-efficient adaptation and is more resilient to the evaluated cross-regional domain shift than the convolutional and Transformer baselines.

title: Geometry-aware dynamic convolutional network for instance-level segmentation of Martian landforms from high-resolution Digital Elevation Model-derived point clouds
abstract: Analysis and interpretation of Martian surface landforms is one of the key topics in deep-space research, offering insights into the planet’s geological evolution and history of water activity. Automated extraction of Martian landforms can greatly assist researchers in rapidly locating and analyzing regions of interest. Therefore, instance segmentation based on remote sensing data represents a promising direction for automation in planetary science. To address the challenges of indistinct landform boundaries and over-segmentation in Martian remote sensing scenes, we propose an end-to-end 3D deep learning instance segmentation framework based on dynamic convolution. In this framework, we incorporate geometric information prediction of Martian landforms to enhance the network’s perception of morphological characteristics, bluewhich improves the separation of adjacent same-class instances. During training, we introduce two feature-space constraints-“pull” and “push” forces-to reduce intra-instance variance while increasing inter-instance separability. The proposed geometry-aware dynamic convolution framework is evaluated on a self-constructed water-formed landform dataset, an impact crater dataset, and a rock dataset from Mars rover perspective and achieves AP of 41.9 ± 0.1%, 63.7 ± 0.3%, and 68.6 ± 0.2%, remaining competitive with recent transformer-based methods such as Mask3D while outperforming clustering- and dynamic-convolution-based baselines. This end-to-end framework provides valuable technical support for subsequent geomorphological interpretation and potential exploration on Mars.

title: A spatially-adaptive automated sample generation framework via multi-source phenological fusion for large-scale crop mapping: demonstrated on peanuts in Shandong, China
abstract: Accurate regional-scale crop mapping is critical for agricultural monitoring but remains persistently hindered by two fundamental challenges: limited inter-class separability arising from the high spectral-temporal similarity of co-occurring crops, and a label scarcity bottleneck exacerbated by the spatial non-stationarity of crop phenology. To address these limitations, this study proposes a novel Spatially-Adaptive Automated Sample Generation (SAASG) framework. By integrating multi-source remote sensing data with an iterative transfer learning strategy, SAASG autonomously generates high-fidelity training samples across heterogeneous landscapes. The framework’s core innovations are twofold. First, we engineer a Multi-source Phenological Feature Curve (MPFC) that synergizes the orthogonal information of Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) backscatter, the optical Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), and a newly developed Contrast-Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (CNDVI). The CNDVI employs a novel spectro-structural modulation mechanism specifically designed to resolve late-season asymptotic saturation. Second, we introduce a Spatially-Adaptive Iterative Domain Adaptation mechanism utilizing a grid-based migration strategy. This discretizes the region into local domains to iteratively propagate phenological knowledge, effectively minimizing domain shift errors through spatial ensemble constraints. Demonstrated on peanuts in Shandong Province, China, the SAASG-generated samples exhibit superior phenological fidelity (Sequence Consistency Score = 0.982 ± 0.008; DTW distance = 0.172 ± 0.050) and possess a statistical distribution statistically congruent with in-situ ground-truth data. Leveraging these automatically labeled samples, we produced a 10-m resolution provincial peanut map with robust accuracy (Overall Accuracy > 0.85) across diverse agro-ecological zones. Crucially, a controlled substitution test confirmed that the classifier trained solely on SAASG samples achieved performance comparable to one trained on labor-intensive field data (ΔOA < 3%). These results confirm that the proposed framework provides a physically interpretable and operationally scalable solution to the training data crisis, enabling reliable large-scale mapping in regions with limited ground observations.

title: InterMine: A foundation model-based multi-task interaction network for remote sensing interpretation of open-pit coal mining activity
abstract: The interpretation of open-pit coal mining activity is critical for resource management and ecological protection. It comprises two key tasks: extent extraction and fine-grained change detection. However, existing methods usually suffer from task separation, and their outputs cannot fully meet the requirements of interpretation. Therefore, this study proposes a foundation model-based multi-task interaction network (InterMine) to jointly perform open-pit mine extent extraction and fine-grained change detection. First, InterMine employs a Siamese foundation model as the encoder to enhance feature representation from images of complex open-pit coal mines and incorporates a channel-spatial feature reconstruction module to adapt the encoded features to meet the semantic and spatial requirements of the decoder. Second, a multi-task interaction mechanism is proposed to facilitate complementary information exchange between tasks. Finally, a consistency loss function based on hard-sample reweighting is designed to mitigate inconsistencies among multi-task outputs. InterMine is trained and evaluated on a self-constructed multi-temporal open-pit coal mining activity interpretation dataset (OMSet). Experimental results demonstrate that InterMine outperforms the compared methods. In particular, InterMine achieves F1-scores of 87.57 %, 83.68 %, and 79.43 % for open-pit mine extent extraction, excavation change detection, and reclamation change detection, respectively, outperforming the comparison methods by 1.89 ∼ 5.29, 3.04 ∼ 7.83, and 2.79 ∼ 7.42 percentage points, respectively. This work provides both technical and data support for open-pit coal mine monitoring. OMSet and the code of InterMine have been made publicly available at https://figshare.com/s/03c029d8e4846faef69f .

title: Image-projected apparent particle size distribution estimation in rock avalanches using direct deep regression from UAV imagery
abstract: Due to the rapid downslope movement of fragmented rock masses, rock avalanches are among the most destructive geomorphic hazards in mountainous regions. Particle size characteristics observed at the surface provide useful information for interpreting fragmentation, transport, and depositional patterns. Recent advances in unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based remote sensing and deep learning have enabled novel methodologies for PSD estimation. However, achieving rapid acquisition and reliable PSD characterization under complex field conditions remains challenging. To address these challenges, we constructed and preprocessed a dedicated UAV dataset for PSD analysis from high-resolution RGB imagery acquired with a DJI Matrice 300 RTK platform. Based on this dataset, we proposed a direct deep regression pipeline to predict characteristic image-projected apparent PSD descriptors, including D 20 , D 40 , D 60 , D 80 , and D max , directly from UAV image patches. The proposed approach was compared with two baseline methods: handcrafted feature-based regression and semantic segmentation-based contour pipelines. Experimental results showed that the direct deep regression pipeline achieved better overall PSD prediction performance than the baseline approaches, with ConvNeXt-Tiny obtaining the lowest mean absolute error (MAE) of 2.23 cm and resolution-normalized MAE of 16.77 ground sampling distance (GSD) units. The model exhibited more stable predictive performance for the intermediate percentiles (D 40 –D 80 ), whereas relatively higher errors were observed for D 20 and D max . The trained model was applied to representative areas within the study deposit to generate spatial maps of surface-visible apparent PSD, demonstrating its potential for UAV-based characterization of surface particle size patterns in fragmented rock deposits. Additional transfer validation on tunnel boring machine (TBM)-excavated rock images provides preliminary evidence of cross-scenario transferability across different material and imaging conditions. True cross-event validation on independent rock avalanche deposits remains to be conducted.

title: A novel framework for urban–rural gradient classification by integrating multidimensional urbanization features via self-supervised learning
abstract: Rapid urbanization has transformed vast natural landscapes into increasingly complex human-dominated environments, giving rise to pronounced urban–rural gradients. However, accurate classification of such gradients remains challenging because biophysical indicators alone cannot fully represent the socioeconomic heterogeneity embedded in the urban–rural continuum. Here, based on multisource Earth observation and geospatial datasets, we propose a novel urban–rural gradient classification framework that integrates multidimensional urbanization features, including, land development, population density, economic intensity, and social vitality, to establish a five-class urban–rural gradient classification scheme-Urban core, Urban area, Suburban area, Rural area, and Natural area. Then, we developed URGCNet, a spatial clustering-driven self-supervised learning model that incorporates ordinal constraints to capture the ordered structure of the urban–rural continuum. Based on this framework, we produced URGCdataset, a 500 m urban–rural gradient classification dataset for mainland China for five benchmark years (2005, 2010, 2015, 2020, and 2025). The framework achieved strong classification performance, with URGCNet reaching an overall accuracy of 91.0% and URGCdataset reaching 93.6% against an independent test sample dataset. Ablation experiments show that removing individual urbanization features reduced the Kappa coefficient by 0.1–0.2, highlighting the indispensable role of socioeconomic information beyond biophysical indicators. Spatiotemporal analysis reveals a clear expansion of human-activity areas over the 2005–2025 period, during which the share of natural areas decreased from 92.7% to 90.0%. Overall, this framework provides a transferable pathway for establishing comparable urban–rural gradient classifications across diverse regional contexts and offers a new spatial foundation for urban environmental and ecological applications.

title: Surface-to-volume physics-informed model for 3D mesoscale eddy detection: Multi-source multi-scale fusion
abstract: Mesoscale eddies play a crucial role in the ocean, and accurate detection of their three-dimensional (3D) structures is essential for understanding marine dynamics. However, 3D eddy reconstruction remains challenging: traditional methods provide limited pixel-level boundary delineation, while existing deep learning approaches suffer from insufficient physical constraints and unrealistic eddy geometries. To address this issue, we propose a surface-to-volume physics-informed model (StV-PI-EddyNet) for extracting 3D mesoscale eddies. We construct a high-quality 3D eddy dataset covering the North Pacific (100°E–100°W, 5°N–65°N) down to 1000 m for model training. The model takes sea surface height (SSH), sea surface temperature (SST), and surface current components (U/V) as inputs and consists of three core modules: 2D feature extraction, 3D feature inversion, and 3D semantic segmentation. It embeds a vorticity prediction branch for physical constraints and uses U-Net-like architectures with spatial and channel attention mechanisms. The loss function combines weighted Dice loss and a vorticity-driven physical loss (mean square error + gradient consistency loss) to ensure high segmentation accuracy and physical consistency. Experimental results show StV-PI-EddyNet model achieves 96.97% global accuracy, 84.80% weighted Dice coefficient, and 0.8955 macro-averaged F1-score. It effectively mitigates boundary distortion issues of existing methods, generating 3D eddy masks with high spatial precision. This model enjoys good scalability and can be further optimized by integrating earth observation advances in architecture design, data sources and application generalization, promoting its in-depth applications in marine and especially underwater dynamic research.

title: VLM-Mapper: Multimodal vision-language models for prior guided lane-level HD map construction
abstract: The automated construction of High-Definition (HD) maps from remote sensing data is essential for modern intelligent transportation systems and spatial data infrastructure. While imagery provides a scalable solution for lane-level HD map construction, traditional discriminative models often struggle in complex scenarios because of their reliance on local visual features and limited use of external geographic context. To address these limitations, this paper introduces VLM-Mapper, a framework that reframes lane-level HD map construction as a multimodal sequence-generation task based on visual–language alignment and prior-conditioned token generation. VLM-Mapper systematically integrates high-resolution aerial imagery with tokenized geographic prior prompts, including standard map metadata and boundary entry points, to guide HD map construction. Furthermore, to mitigate the spatial inconsistencies and count errors of autoregressive decoding, we implement a two-stage post-training pipeline. This strategy establishes spatial alignment via Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT), followed by a Reinforcement Learning (RL) phase using Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with a custom geometry-aware and numerical reward function. Experimental results on the large-scale OpenSatMap dataset show that VLM-Mapper achieves state-of-the-art performance and improves the robustness and topological consistency of HD map construction across large-scale aerial imagery.

title: Breaking modal barriers: Achieving modality-balanced semantic segmentation across optical and SAR images through optical image-supervised learning
abstract: As the two primary imaging modalities in remote sensing, optics and Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) have been widely applied in semantic segmentation tasks. However, the scarcity of annotated samples in SAR images limits the performance of related models. How to leverage the abundant annotated samples of optical images to achieve modality-balanced semantic segmentation capabilities across both optical and SAR modalities is of great significance for all-weather interpretation. Restricted by the complexity of modality perception, achieving balanced cross-modal segmentation still faces significant challenges. To address the above issues, we fully consider the modal balance and reliability of knowledge transfer in modal migration and propose a modality-balanced knowledge distillation (MBKD) transfer learning framework. By generating and learning virtual modalities and stitched modalities, a cross-modal migration task is transformed into two symmetric intra-modal migration subtasks, explicitly promoting balanced knowledge transfer between modalities. To demonstrate the effectiveness and practicality of the proposed framework, we conducted application experiments on the large-scale public dataset WHU-OPT-SAR, MULTISENGE-6, and in 6 provinces of China. The results show that our method significantly outperforms other approaches in terms of both performance and stability.

title: Enhancing soil property retrieval in an Ali-Perudic Argosols–dominated region through multi-angle hyperspectral feature integration
abstract: Soil bidirectional reflectance distribution function (BRDF) is strongly influenced by soil physicochemical properties, yet most hyperspectral retrieval studies rely on single-view reflectance, leaving the value of multi-angle information insufficiently explored. In this study, bidirectional reflectance factors (BRFs) were measured at 48 viewing angles for 156 soil samples collected from a region dominated by Ali-Perudic Argosols. An optimal multi-angle retrieval framework was developed for different soil properties by systematically comparing spectral preprocessing methods, feature extraction, and modeling algorithms. The effects of viewing angle on retrieval accuracy and feature wavelength distribution were further analyzed, and the applicability of simulated multi-angle BRFs generated using SOILSPECT model was further assessed. Results show that the optimal framework for single-view reflectance combines Savitzky–Golay (SG) smoothing, a hybrid random frog–competitive adaptive reweighted sampling (RFROG–CARS) feature selection strategy, and nonlinear support vector machine (SVM) regression. Retrieval accuracy varied substantially with viewing geometry, and no universal optimal viewing angle was identified across soil properties. For multi-angle BRF data, a two-dimensional convolutional neural network (2D-CNN) feature extraction approach outperformed the RFROG–CARS wavelength selection method. Specifically, R 2 (RMSE) improved from 0.64 (8.8 g/kg) to 0.73 (7.7 g/kg) for SOM content, from 0.53 (6.9 %) to 0.61 (6.3 %) for sand content, and from 0.64 (4.7 %) to 0.69 (4.4 %) for silt content, while remaining comparable for cation exchange capacity (0.77/2.4 cmol/kg to 0.76/2.4 cmol/kg) and clay content (0.80/4.3 % to 0.79/4.3 %). Although the retrieval accuracy based on multi-angle BRFs remained slightly lower than that obtained from the optimal viewing geometry, it consistently outperformed most individual viewing angles. The selected multi-angle hyperspectral features were distributed across nearly all viewing angles, indicating complementary spectral–geometric information. Although retrieval accuracy based on simulated BRFs was lower than that based on measured BRFs, the results were broadly comparable. These findings support the use of multi-angle information in soil spectroscopy and remote sensing applications.

title: PRINT: A semi-empirical canopy water removal approach for improving estimates of leaf nitrogen and grain protein contents in winter wheat
abstract: Accurate estimation of leaf nitrogen content (LNC) and grain protein content (GPC) in winter wheat is crucial for making fertilization recommendations and assessing grain quality. Previous methods primarily relied on chlorophyll (Chl)-sensitive vegetation indices from the visible and near-infrared domain, while shortwave-infrared spectral features linked to dry matter and nitrogen remain underutilized due to strong leaf water masking. Although existing water removal methods can mitigate the absorption effects of leaf water, the reliability of the resulting simulated dry-canopy reflectance spectra (SDR) is limited by inaccurate leaf mass per area (LMA) retrieval. This study aimed to develop a semi-empirical water removal approach by integrating PRior knowledge and INitialization of leaf water conTent and LMA (PRINT) to simulate SDR, with the objective of improving the estimation performance of LNC and GPC. To achieve this goal, a Random Forest-based hybrid retrieval model was developed to increase LMA retrieval accuracy. Meanwhile, a visible and shortwave-based nitrogen index (VSNI) by combining the visible (proxy of Chl) and shortwave-infrared features was proposed for improving estimation performance of LNC and GPC. Moreover, experimental datasets covering multiple growth stages and geographic sites were collected to improve sample representativeness. These datasets were utilized to improve the retrieval of LMA and evaluate the performance of LNC and GPC estimations. The results demonstrated that the PRINT significantly improved the estimation accuracy of LMA over two standard physically-based inversion models (RMSE: 6.23 g/m 2 vs 8.25 g/m 2 and 45.73 g/m 2 ). Compared with existing VI-based models, the VSNI-based models yielded substantial improvements in LNC (R 2 : 0.62 ∼ 0.65, RMSE = 0.42 ∼ 0.54%) across sites, and enhanced GPC estimation accuracy up to R 2 = 0.66 (RMSE = 0.70%) at the peak filling stage across two years at one site. The proposed methodology advances the spectroscopic understanding of shortwave-infrared responses to nitrogen-related agronomic biochemicals, and holds significant potential for future applications in large-scale growth monitoring of wheat systems using satellite imagery.

title: High-resolution mapping of urban wet-bulb temperature and its intra-urban variability: A London case study
abstract: Most extreme-heat studies map high-resolution near-surface dry-bulb air temperature ( T a ), yet wet-bulb temperature ( T w ) fields that can capture the combined effects of T a and humidity to represent human heat stress remain limited. This data gap constrains investigation of intra-urban heat variability and the timing of peak heat stress. Here, based on the Rankine-Kirchhoff approximations of Romps, this study innovatively generates hourly 1-km T w by integrating crowdsourced station observations with remote sensing and reanalysis data in machine learning based downscaling frameworks. Taking London during the summers of 2019–2022 as a case study, the tuned RF-based downscaling approach achieved the best performance ( MAE = 0.65 °C, RMSE = 0.93 °C, R 2 = 0.91) among all models. The resulting T w patterns diverge from those commonly reported for T a : blue infrastructure shows no consistent cooling effect, whereas vegetated areas cool T w increasingly as tree cover rises, pointing to tree-dominated green infrastructure as a promising humid-heat countermeasure. Results further show that daily maximum T w occurs 0.7 h earlier than daily maximum T a in London, opposite to findings elsewhere, implying that climate type and coastal influence modulate the timing of peak T w , which may affect the attribution of excess nighttime mortality. Besides, a systematic global assessment of the mechanisms controlling T w extremes is also required in the future.

title: Remote sensing of lake surface water temperature reveals divergent hydroclimatic associations with lake ice phenology across China
abstract: Lake ice phenology is a sensitive indicator of climate change, yet its regional hydroclimatic associations remain poorly understood. Here, we reconstructed daily lake surface water temperature (LSWT) from MODIS for 583 lakes across China and derived freeze-up date (FUD), break-up date (BUD), and ice cover duration (ICD) for 376 seasonally ice-covered lakes. Robustness was evaluated with sensitivity tests, meteorological observations, transition-period comparisons, and passive-microwave ice records; Mann-Kendall tests, Theil-Sen slopes, VIF-constrained XGBoost-SHAP, and structural equation modeling assessed trends and regional associations. FUD was delayed in all three ice-covered regions, whereas BUD was delayed in the Tibetan Plateau Lake Region (TPR) but advanced in the Mongolian-Xinjiang Lake Region (MXR) and Northeast Lake Region (NLR), resulting in shorter ICD in all regions. Regional mean ICD declined by 0.03, 0.35, and 0.47 d yr -1 in the TPR, MXR, and NLR, respectively; significant lake-level changes were concentrated in the TPR, with 72 and 33 lakes showing significant FUD and BUD trends. All nine models retained positive hold-out R 2 (0.535–0.960). SHAP attributions differed by region: radiative variables dominated in the TPR, the MXR showed metric-specific associations with wind, snowfall, geographic, and thermal , and geographic, radiative, and morphometric variables dominated in the NLR. Structural equation models indicated stronger precipitation-related associations in the NLR and snowfall-related associations in the MXR and TPR. These results reveal pronounced regional heterogeneity in lake ice responses to warming and the value of integrating remote sensing, interpretable machine learning, and pathway modeling to resolve these contrasts.

title: A retrieval method for passive microwave LST integrating radiative transfer-informed land-air environmental conditions
abstract: Passive microwave (PMW) remote sensing is a significant data source for generating spatiotemporally continuous land surface temperature (LST). Although empirical methods can retrieve PMW LST that approximates the physical meaning of thermal infrared (TIR)-derived LST, they generally fail to fully consider land-air variables implied by PMW radiative transfer principles. Particularly, the impacts of atmospheric situation have often been overlooked. Here, we propose a machine learning-based retrieval method that integrates a broader range of land-air environmental variables in accordance with PMW radiative transfer principles (PLST-ILA). Validation against pre-extracted MODIS LST shows that the proposed method achieves annual daytime and nighttime root mean square errors (RMSEs) of 3.17 K and 2.21 K, respectively, showing reductions of 9.9 %∼26.1 % relative to the five reference methods. Validation at six in-situ sites indicates that PLST-ILA yields an annual daytime RMSE of 4.21 K and a nighttime RMSE of 4.02 K, reducing the daytime RMSE by 0.33 ∼ 1.68 K and the nighttime RMSE by 0.27 ∼ 1.32 K benchmarked by four advanced methods. The monthly-scale model generally achieves superior performance compared with the seasonal-scale and annual-scale models. Moreover, accounting for topographic and geomorphological characteristics, anthropogenic emissions, atmospheric humidity, and aerosol optical depth may further improve retrieval accuracy. Finally, the proposed method demonstrates the capability to reconstruct PMW observations within orbital gaps. Validation against gap-retained MODIS LST yields annual RMSEs of 3.68 K during the daytime and 2.69 K at night. The results of this study provide a technical reference for PMW LST retrieval and may contribute to optimizing the precision of thermal-related research.

title: The Bovine Slurry Index (BSI): An integrated framework for manure pond mapping using GeoFM-derived cattle-operation detection and Sentinel-2 spectral formulation
abstract: Quantifying greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from livestock operations is a prerequisite for reconciling bottom-up inventories with atmospheric observations. However, global GHG reporting remains limited by a lack of spatially explicit data on animal waste management systems (AWMS), forcing reliance on coarse regional assumptions rather than operation-level observations. Existing geospatial foundation models partly address this spatial gap by mapping cattle-operation footprints that provide upstream spatial context, but contextual detection alone cannot identify the manure-management features within them. To address this gap, we introduce the Bovine Slurry Index (BSI), an empirical Sentinel-2 spectral index for detecting liquid/slurry manure ponds within known cattle-operation footprints. The primary formulation, BSI-E, uses calibrated narrow-NIR (B8A) and SWIR-1 (B11) reflectance bounds derived from manure pond samples in the United States and China. The index targets the empirically observed intermediate NIR-SWIR response of manure ponds relative to clear water, vegetation, dry holding pens, and exposed soil. Calibration used 2,730 pond samples from the U.S. and China, and segmentation was evaluated against 945 reference polygons across all five geographic regions. BSI-E produced stronger pond-to-background contrast and higher segmentation accuracy than evaluated water indices, with dataset-level intersection-over-union (IoU) ranging from 0.26 in Brazil to 0.68 in the United States and precision reaching 0.91. Optimal thresholds varied geographically from 0.25 to 1.00, and performance was strongest in dryland feedlot systems and lower in humid or spectrally mixed settings. BSI provides a target-specific spectral method for generating operation-scale evidence that could inform AWMS activity data within these footprints.

title: Assessing forest structural dynamics and post-disturbance early-stage recovery using PlanetScope imagery and photogrammetric point clouds
abstract: Forests in the southeastern United States (US) are frequently disturbed by wind events, such as hurricanes, tornadoes, and severe windstorms, affecting ecosystem resilience, biodiversity, and carbon storage. Monitoring post-disturbance forest changes is challenging due to the limited availability of spatially continuous and temporally high-resolution canopy height data. To address these limitations, we evaluated the potential of PlanetScope data to assess forest structure and thematic changes across three wind-affected sites in the southeastern US: Oakmulgee (tornado), Flagg Mountain (straight-line wind), and Weeks Bay (hurricane). We used multi-stereo PlanetScope imagery to generate photogrammetric point clouds, which were processed to extract a suite of discrete canopy height metrics at different spatial resolutions (3 m, 10 m, 15 m, and 20 m) and validated using airborne lidar-derived canopy height metrics. Random Forest (RF) regression models were then developed using PlanetScope imagery, acquired concurrently with airborne lidar across study sites, and the trained models were applied to produce pre- and post-disturbance canopy height maps. Similarly, RF classification models were developed for three scenarios (airborne lidar acquisition date, pre-wind, and post-wind), and applied to generate forest/non-forest maps for pre- and post-disturbance periods, enabling assessment of thematic changes following wind disturbance. Results indicate that upper canopy height percentiles (95th and 98th) aggregated at a 20 m grid resolution produced the strongest agreement with airborne lidar measurements (correlation coefficient (r) = 0.32–0.33, Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) = 7.57–9.05 m). When the comparison was limited to grid cells where PlanetScope and lidar heights differed by 7 m or less, agreement improved (r = 0.68–0.79, RMSE = 3.70–4.35 m). RF canopy height estimation models showed moderate accuracy across study sites (R 2 = 0.51–0.54, RMSE = 2.45–4.31 m). Multi-temporal analysis using generated 20 m canopy height maps revealed substantial canopy height reductions after wind disturbance, affecting 40.47% of Oakmulgee site, 36.52% of Flagg Mountain, and 60.92% of Weeks Bay. Overall, the approach provides a promising framework for assessing and monitoring forest disturbance impacts. It captures post-disturbance changes in forest structure with an ability to provide spatially explicit and timely information on canopy structure and thematic dynamics, particularly in areas where airborne lidar or field measurements are limited.
